result.title: BLANC: Adaptive Temporal Scheduling for Sign Language Production
result.summary: Sign language production (SLP) aims to synthesize expressive signing motion from written text. Modeling signing motion presents two key temporal challenges. First, fine-grained hand articulations demand higher temporal resolution than relatively slower body movements. Second, signing events unfold over variable durations, calling for adaptive temporal scheduling during generation. To address these challenges, we first introduce a Multi-Rate Vector Quantizer (MRVQ), an articulation-decoupled motion tokenizer that represents the body and both hands as separate discrete streams at distinct temporal resolutions. Building on this representation, we propose BLANC (BLock-wise Adaptive diffusioN with Articulatory Clock), a gloss-free SLP framework that generates variable-duration motion blocks causally while denoising tokens in parallel within each block. At its core, a Latent Articulatory Clock (LAC) learns temporal structure from multi-scale motion-derived partitions to predict block durations and sequence termination during generation. We further introduce inference-time body-conditioned hand refinement to improve coordination across articulators. Extensive experiments on PHOENIX-2014T and CSL-Daily demonstrate that BLANC achieves state-of-the-art performance in sign language production.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文研究手语生成：提出多速率矢量量化器 MRVQ，把身体与双手表示为不同时间分辨率的离散动作流，并在此基础上构建免 gloss 的块级扩散框架 BLANC，用 Latent Articulatory Clock 预测可变时长运动块及序列终止，在 PHOENIX-2014T 与 CSL-Daily 上报告了领先结果。
AI.relevance_reason: 手语动作生成与 VLM 推理相距较远，但其以 latent 时钟变量预测生成块时长与终止的机制，可能为 LVR 中动态计算预算与 STOP 决策的建模提供类比线索，可供核查。
